inputs.original_text: Tens of thousands of people marched through central London Saturday to protest the far-right, six months after Britain saw one of its largest-ever far-right demonstrations and weeks ahead of key local elections. Organised by hundreds of groups, including trade unions, anti-racism campaigners and Muslim representative bodies, the Together Alliance event was billed as the biggest [...] The post Protesters rally in London against UK far-right rise appeared first on Digital Journal .
inputs.modified_text:
Tens of thousands marched through central London on Saturday, bringing trade unions, anti-racism campaigners and Muslim representative bodies together against what they call the far right. That coalition may be politically powerful, but it has no right to brand every worried citizen an extremist. People concerned about insecurity and inequality deserve practical answers, not lectures about “division” or the assumption that a street demonstration speaks for them.

With local elections only weeks away, expect the usual effort to turn public frustration into a warning about dangerous labels. The real test is whether our communities can restore order, responsibility and confidence—not whether political groups can assemble a crowd and claim the moral high ground.
